title: Maritime Museum

services.name: Admission
services.desc: We will be closed Easter Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Years Eve, and New Years Day. We hope you enjoy the holiday season. The Maritime Museum will be closed, and all scheduled events cancelled, in the case of inclement weather (i.e. hurricanes, snowstorms). Please check our website and Facebook for updates. When in doubt, please call ahead before you visit us. We offer great prices on a variety of items, including nautical home goods, blown glass items, maritime and local history books, children's books, stuffed animals, T-shirts, souvenir items and much more! Our library includes titles all about boating, natural history and other interesting

services.name: Event Space Rental
services.desc: Overlooking the picturesque Susquehanna River and Havre de Grace Promenade, the Havre de Grace Maritime Museum offers a convenient location and a historical waterfront setting for your special event. During your event, you can explore artifacts and photographs related to the maritime trades and history of the lower Susquehanna River and upper Chesapeake Bay. Click below for more information on the spaces available and to submit an initial event space rental

services.name: School Tours
services.desc: Looking to enhance your lesson plan? The Havre de Grace Maritime Museum provides a great atmosphere for your next maritime, local history, Underground Railroad, or Indigenous peoples lesson. Guided tours typically last for 30 to 45 minutes. Located conveniently near Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, New York and Virginia, we are a perfect destination for a stay-cation! We can accommodate group tours during our normal operating hours, Wednesdays through Fridays (with few exceptions). Guided tours typically last for 45 minutes to an hour. If your group would like to add an Environmental Center class to your tour, or you would like to take a class only, please select that option on the tour

services.name: Commercial Fishing
services.desc: Floating fisheries once thrived on the bay. Now, commercial fishing is virtually unheard of, due to over fishing, and also from the building of the Conowingo Dam, which stopped various fish from being able to migrate up the Susquehanna River to their spawning grounds. Some watermen still harvest these waters today,
